feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited quantified outcomes beyond traffic/platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility through concrete platforms, tools, and scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, GA4/BigQuery/Power BI).  
- Writing is polished and audience-appropriate, with a strong headline and relevant recent-project examples that reinforce strategic and technical range.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and scannability. The footer “Recent Projects” also feels unusually placed and would work better as a dedicated section.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: improvements in engagement, efficiency, search performance, email results, production savings, or campaign impact would strengthen impact.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation is inconsistent around slash usage and list formatting; “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—prefer “French (A2, improving)” or similar. No major misspellings detected.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. Tightening it will improve scanability and sharpen differentiation.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct phrasing like “leading digital platforms, governance, and content operations for.”
- Add one concrete scale signal from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Streamline the second sentence to emphasize current-value strengths: enterprise web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, and AI-enabled search/UX.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Drives enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled search experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with footer project detail and core competencies; “AI-enabled search experiences” is more specific.
- “Multimedia production” is repeated across competencies and experience; keep it only if it’s essential to target roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and grouped around senior-level outcomes rather than adjacent skill labels.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; e.g., use noun phrases consistently: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure
- Replace broader or vaguer items with more specific, senior-level language tied to recent work: AI-enabled search and discovery • Workflow automation and cross-platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications operations” for “Multi-channel digital communications leadership” to better reflect scope and seniority
- Refine the last item to “Multimedia production, livestreaming, and studio operations” for clarity and consistency

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; this section should be shorter or more differentiated
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills’ “Public-sector and advocacy messaging”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently: project name + action + result/purpose.
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong, but simplify where possible and keep parallel structure across all entries.
- Use consistent punctuation/style: add commas in series, spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently, and avoid repeating “built/developed” in every item.
- If available, add one concrete outcome, audience, or scale marker to 1–2 projects for stronger impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in recent NACo roles.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider prioritizing unique projects here rather than restating core responsibilities.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps heavily with your NACo director role and recent projects. Tighten it around consulting scope, senior advisory value, and 1–2 concrete outcomes or named initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper consulting summary: “Advise the National Association of Counties on digital strategy, content operations, Drupal platform enhancements, and enterprise web modernization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g. “Built cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet more outcome-oriented: mention launched microsites, reusable content modules, member toolkits, or improved publishing efficiency if measurable.
- Rephrase the AI work as a flagship initiative: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content models, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats themes already covered in the 2022–2024 director role.
- Specific projects like AI search and microsites may duplicate the “Recent Projects” section; keep this entry higher-level unless you add results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the adjacent NACo roles on newsletters, video, and day-to-day channel management.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s enterprise digital communications function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make analytics/governance results more concrete: add reporting speed, decision-making cadence, publishing consistency, or stakeholder adoption if available.
- Rephrase channel/video bullets toward strategic ownership, not execution: “Scaled in-house multimedia capacity by launching NACo’s first broadcast-quality studio…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems.
- Video expansion also appears in earlier NACo roles; frame this here as building infrastructure/capacity, not producing recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scale so it shows how this role set up the later director-level impact.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Ran day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with concrete coordination/process language: “Built cross-team editorial planning routines and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this role focused on execution, coordination and channel growth rather than leadership/governance.
- Weekly video/newsletter points also echo the 2015–2018 role; emphasize expansion/operationalization here, not initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around the candidate’s most senior, recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Keep terminology aligned with recent roles: emphasize governance, web modernization, and content operations over “messaging,” which feels less differentiated here.
- Use parallel noun phrases and avoid filler like “focused”; “audience-centered content strategy” is cleaner than “audience-focused content planning.”
- If space allows, consider “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications” as a stronger lead item.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; keep this only if other skills are trimmed elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Put the most relevant, recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve detailed tools like SharePoint, Power Pages, and jQuery for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; consider keeping it in only one place unless it is a signature differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This section should emphasize higher-value analytical leadership, not repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy & measurement frameworks
- KPI design and executive reporting
- Dashboarding and insight generation
- Web performance, SEO and user behavior analysis
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity
- Put the most senior/value-add items first: KPI design, executive reporting, insight generation, then tools.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “C-suite/leadership dashboards” for clearer business language.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented phrase tied to recent work elsewhere, such as “analytics infrastructure for 10,000+ page web platform.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the Technical + IT “Data, Analytics & Optimization” list almost exactly.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may partially overlap with broader digital strategy language unless framed as analytics-specific.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it sharper by emphasizing higher-value, recent capabilities and using more specific phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, more senior wording: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Post-production editing”
- Lead with event delivery and studio capability, since recent roles highlight building an in-house studio and supporting advocacy/event programming.
- Consider swapping “virtual” for “broadcast” or “multi-camera” to sound more distinctive and less dated.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill area to outcomes in experience bullets rather than listing broad terms here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrase verbatim.
- “Video production and editing” overlaps with “Multimedia & Creative Tools” and several NACo bullets; keep this section capability-focused, not task-focused.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s generic and slightly redundant with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is clearly the strongest/recent platform, lead with that and consider adding light proficiency context.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.
- If space allows, add a qualifier to show depth: **Drupal (migration, microsites, governance)** rather than a bare product list.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use either **CMS platforms** or **Web Platforms & CMS**, not both in different sections.
- If you want stronger impact, replace the standalone list with: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider trimming one section or differentiating this one as platform names only.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight versus the rest unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding basics to applied implementation: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery)”
- Group tools by function for clarity: “API integrations • Tag management (Google Tag Manager) • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • CI/CD and version control (GitHub Actions, Git/GitHub)”
- If accurate, add one higher-value recent capability tied to current work, e.g. “structured search implementation” or “technical troubleshooting for Drupal environments”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless used elsewhere consistently; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing
- “API integrations” and workflow-related tooling also overlap with Topline Skills and Automation & Workflow Systems

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize systems ownership, e.g. **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems**.
- Tighten and group by function: **Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier** | **Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp** | **Slack, Microsoft Teams**.
- Put the strongest/recent tools first; if Airtable/Power Automate were central to NACo workflow design, keep them leading.
- If space allows, add light context instead of just names: **Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project operations: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they were meaningfully used to run cross-team operations.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platforms, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the strategic email/engagement angle shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise-scale communications systems, not just list tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email, member communications and campaign journey platforms)**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses: **used for newsletters, audience segmentation, automated journeys and member engagement communications**
- Keep ordering by strongest/recent relevance; if Dynamics 365 is most current/strategic, leave it first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; avoid repeating outcomes here.
- “Engagement” also partially overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations,” so keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and recent NACo experience. Make it tighter, more capability-led, and only keep tools that reinforce current senior-level strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation**
- Replace “A/B testing” with **Experimentation** unless you’ve directly run formal test programs; it reads more credible at senior level.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with **KPI reporting** or **Executive reporting** to emphasize business use, not just output format.
- Order by strongest/recent tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This line substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills: Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one version or making this section tools-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split the second sentence into concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped expand the organization’s in-house digital content capacity.”
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, web traffic impact, or turnaround/time-saved from improved workflows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or early development of the format.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; here, specify foundational processes or team setup instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, initiative, and any concrete outputs or audiences.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; partnered across teams to turn research into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specific deliverables if known: web features, reports, interviews, audio episodes, or campaign materials.
- Add scale where possible: number of projects supported, podcast episodes produced, stakeholders served, or turnaround improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing broad “digital content production” since later roles already cover web, video, email, and multimedia leadership in more depth.
- Don’t repeat “first in-house digital team” or later video/livestream accomplishments here.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed capability list than a tight tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should stay software-focused and concise.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to emphasize actual tools first, then a short production capability tag.
- Use parallel phrasing and tighten generic terms like “Livestream studio workflows.”
- If true, add platform specificity for stronger credibility.

Suggested edit:
- Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator
